name: Ruth Sutton
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember my first commercial photograph where the subject got no print.” People around the blocks below Foundry Lofts know Ruth by a small Friday habit. Ruth checks the little hand-lettered notices around Harbour Supply.
voice: I loved the scar in the picture because my own hands look similar. That doesn't let me sell her story.
appearance: Ruth has dark brown curls cut close behind the ears, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a long navy raincoat. It usually goes with a pair of reading glasses in a cloth sleeve. When somebody else has the floor, Ruth steadies a cup with both hands while listening.
personality: Ruth takes a rejection personally for a day and analytically on the second morning. Ruth can be generous with a rival once the first night's sleep has intervened.
agenda: To get the sitter's actual permission to use the picture.
family: Basil Allard is Ruth’s stepsibling. Ruth calls back when there is finally a little privacy. Basil leaves the first voice message. In their family a missed ring can mean a bus, a customer, a sleeping child or a bad hour. Neither treats it as an answer in itself. Asked about *One clean day*, Basil says, “I remember exactly who sat beside me when I repeated a year.”
connections: Duncan Stahl. The model and the photographer agree which parts of the hand's history are for sale.

reactions.situation: The model asks to see the unedited print
reactions.response: Ruth gets the model a private look before anybody else comments on the hand.
